name: Team
simple: A Team is a group players can belong to, like Red Team or Blue Team. Each Team has a color. Players on a team get their name shown in that color and are grouped together in the player list. Team objects must live inside the Teams service.
analogy: A Team is like a jersey color in a school sports day. Everyone wearing red is on the Red Team, sits together on the scoreboard, and starts at the red starting line (red SpawnLocations).
whenToUse: Split players into sides for a game (cops vs robbers, red vs blue).
Count or loop over everyone on one side (GetPlayers).
Make team-only spawn points or team-only doors.
where: Inside the Teams service. Add them in Studio (hover Teams, click +, insert Team) or with `Instance.new("Team")` parented to `game:GetService("Teams")`. Players join a team by setting `player.Team`.

terms.TeamColor: The BrickColor that identifies a team. Many team features match things by this color, so give every team a different one.
terms.BrickColor: One of Roblox's named colors, like "Bright red" or "Lapis".
terms.auto-assign: Roblox putting a joining player on a team by itself, choosing the team with the fewest players.
terms.SpawnLocation: A pad where players appear. It can be locked to one team's color.

examples.title: Create two teams and balance players yourself
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local Teams = game:GetService("Teams")

local function makeTeam(name, colorName)
    local team = Instance.new("Team")
    team.Name = name
    team.TeamColor = BrickColor.new(colorName)
    team.AutoAssignable = false -- we'll choose teams ourselves
    team.Parent = Teams
    return team
end

local red = makeTeam("Red Team", "Bright red")
local blue = makeTeam("Blue Team", "Bright blue")

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    -- Put the new player on whichever team has fewer people
    if #red:GetPlayers() <= #blue:GetPlayers() then
        player.Team = red
    else
        player.Team = blue
    end
end)

red.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    print(player.Name .. " joined the Red Team")
end)
explain: Each Team gets a name and a unique TeamColor, and is parented to the Teams service.
AutoAssignable = false stops Roblox from choosing teams for us.
GetPlayers() gives the list of a team's players; # counts them.
Setting player.Team moves the player onto that team, which fires the team's PlayerAdded event.

gotchas: Teams only work when they're directly inside the Teams service.
Give every team a different TeamColor. Spawns and Player.TeamColor match teams by color.
AutoAssignable only evens out teams when players join, not when they leave.
Teams don't block friendly fire on their own. Check teams in your weapon scripts.

Team.AutoAssignable.simple: If true, new players can be placed on this team automatically. Roblox picks the auto-assignable team with the fewest players. If no team allows it, players join as neutral.
Team.AutoAssignable.example: team.AutoAssignable = false -- only scripts put people on this team

Team.AutoColorCharacters.simple: Old — it no longer does anything. Color characters yourself with a script if you want.

Team.Score.simple: Old — use a leaderstats leaderboard instead.

Team.TeamColor.simple: The team's color. Players on the team get this color as their Player.TeamColor, their name shows in it, and SpawnLocations with the same TeamColor belong to this team.

Team:GetPlayers.simple: Gives a list of all players on this team right now.
Team:GetPlayers.example:
for _, player in team:GetPlayers() do
    print(player.Name .. " is on " .. team.Name)
end
print(team.Name .. " has " .. #team:GetPlayers() .. " players")

Team.PlayerAdded.simple: Fires when a player joins this team. Gives you that player.

Team.PlayerRemoved.simple: Fires when a player leaves this team: they switched teams, became neutral, or left the game.
